A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PCA framework and dataset, renamed from PCA-D to ChatSOP. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and complete appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original SOP-prediction and dialogue-generation experiments in Tables 4–5, human evaluations in Table 6, and dataset-quality assessments.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental results in Tables 4–5 and Figure 4, alongside dataset-quality assessments and the appendix cost comparison.

M1.justification: The offline-planning and SOP-guided MCTS framework remains. However, v1's fixed reward 0.5(LLM + 0.5 state) becomes a parameterized reward with lambda explicitly set to 1, eliminating the task-completion term as written. Final action selection also changes from highest UCT to highest Q. These are localized revisions to the stated procedure; rerunning the experiments is not established.

E1.justification: Both versions retain Chinese SOP prediction and dialogue generation, 53 tasks and 3,114 dialogues. The reported domain count changes from 45 to 32, and v2 supplies a domain/task inventory. Without a corresponding v1 inventory or an explanation of the revision, actual coverage changes cannot be distinguished from regrouping or correction.

E2.justification: V2 substantially narrows automatic dialogue comparisons: it removes CoT+SFT for all four open models, MCTS without SOP for both large open models, and Qwen1.5-72b ToT/ToT+SOP comparisons from v1 Table 5. Matching relocated material shows that Llama3-70b ToT comparisons remain in Figure 4 and an SFT cost/success comparison remains in Figure 12. AL becoming DAL is only a rename.

E3.justification: Table 3 changes the reported validation-dialogue count from 309 to 324, and BLEU-2/4 evaluation is removed. Dataset cross-annotation changes from a 20% sample to every instance. V2 also introduces a general temperature/top-p statement of 0.1/0.1 that conflicts with its retained appendix dialogue settings of 1/0.95; an actual sampling change or rerun cannot be inferred.

E4.justification: Removing the MCTS-without-SOP results eliminates the direct MCTS ablation isolating SOP's contribution on Qwen1.5-72b and Llama3-70b. The identity-verification and persuasion cases remain, with edited wording and presentation. The ToT and cost plots largely redisplay existing comparisons rather than establish new analyses.

E5.justification: Both retain five-fold cross-validation for SOP prediction and report point estimates without seed counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. V2's new IAA value of 0.88 reports an outcome of the already-described agreement checking; no new statistical estimator or uncertainty-reporting procedure is specified.

E6.justification: Corresponding SOP scores and retained dialogue-accuracy rows are unchanged: GPT-3.5 CoT and MCTS+SOP action accuracies remain 48.57 and 76.52, so the highlighted 27.95-point gap is not a version-to-version gain. Nevertheless, v2 removes substantial result content, including all BLEU scores, several automatic comparison rows and some human-evaluation metrics. It adds raw-sample accuracy of 0.91, IAA of 0.88 and dataset action proportions.

T1.justification: V2 Equation 6 replaces v1 Equation 7's fixed reward definition with a lambda-dependent function and a non-equivalent stated setting. This changes a mathematical definition beyond notation. The adjacency-list reformulation otherwise largely restates the existing graph task, and neither version introduces theoretical proofs.

C1.justification: V2 foregrounds controllability and recasts dataset novelty as providing the first intermediate SOP annotations, additionally suggesting applicability to general-purpose LLM-agent evaluation. V1 foregrounds the jointly proactive and controllable dialogue problem. The central framework, dataset and MCTS contributions remain, while the abstract's numerical improvement highlights existing results.

C2.justification: V1 attributes rare knowledge errors to providing task-related knowledge in Section 6.3; v2 interprets high knowledge accuracy as evidence that the models possess sufficient task knowledge in Section 6.4. The explanations of the two dialogue cases and the hallucination and runtime limitations are otherwise retained.

D1.justification: V2 replaces the resource placeholder with a concrete repository address and substantially expands annotation recruitment, compensation, tool and guideline documentation. It adds the domain/task inventory, SFT batch size of 128, and detailed human-scoring rules, including coherence weights. Conversely, descriptions of edit-distance SOP-subpath matching, path-loop handling and tiktoken measurement are omitted. These are documentation changes, not evidence that every underlying procedure changed.

R1.justification: V2 adds references including the GPT-4 report, LARA, Brownian-bridge dialogue planning and the schema-guided dialogue dataset, while removing several persuasion, negotiation and annotation references such as CaSiNo and Gilardi et al. The central positioning around SOP constraints and MCTS remains; moving conversational-agent background into Related Work is primarily structural.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, formulation, method and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten and reorganized. The title changes, PCA-D becomes ChatSOP, and terminology is standardized. The appendices are substantially restructured, with separate annotation, evaluation and prompt sections rather than merely adding scientific content.

P2.justification: Figures 1–3 are redesigned, and the human-results table and case display are replaced by a combined radar/bar-chart and dialogue figure. Tables receive separate metric columns and shading. Appendix listings become illustrated snippets and colored prompt boxes, with an annotation-tool screenshot and cost chart added. The original SOP example is retained as renumbered Figure 10.

improvement.justification: V2 improves organization, annotation documentation, scoring transparency and resource-access information. However, it removes important fine-tuned and no-SOP comparisons, while the changed reward description is not reconciled with retained scores. Its new claim of superiority across all metrics also conflicts with Table 5's Qwen1.5-72b dialogue accuracy: 29.32 for MCTS+SOP versus 30.72 for CoT+SOP. These documentation gains and weakened or ambiguous scientific reporting prevent a confident net-quality judgment.
